hypotheses.justification: The statement is still true for N = ∅. Take n = 0 and z the empty family, so Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range z) is just the image of k in K. The first conjunct is vacuous. The second says that any f ∈ K lying in Q.toValuationSubring for every place Q is algebraic over k. Since k is algebraically closed, such an f then lies in k. A Place is a nontrivial discrete valuation subring of K containing k. Here K is a function field of one variable over the algebraically closed field k: it is essentially of finite type, and Ω[K/k] is free of rank 1, so the transcendence degree is 1. Suppose f is transcendental over k. Then K is finite over k(f). Take the integral closure of k[1/f] in K, which is a Dedekind domain. A prime over (1/f) gives a place Q with f ∉ Q.toValuationSubring. This uses the same ofHeightOneSpectrum and integral-closure machinery as holRing_fg, with 1/f in place of t. So the empty-N case is the classical fact that functions regular on the whole curve are constant. The proof therefore needs a short case split on N = ∅. In that case, use n = 0 and the argument above, or the degree-zero property of principal divisors together with finite residue fields. For nonempty N, proceed as before. hN is used only to feed holRing_fg and exists_fn, which pick a place Q₀ ∈ N, so it is a proof convenience and not needed for the truth of the statement.
